title: Assessment of Tariff-impact on Singapore's Trade Sectors following US' Section 301 Investigations
what_it_is: Assessment of Tariff-impact on Singapore's Trade Sectors following US' Section 301 Investigations

sections.label: US Section 301 investigations Singapore
sections.summary: The US Trade Representative initiated two Section 301 investigations in March 2026, and MTI clarified the US ran a US$27 billion trade surplus with Singapore in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On 11 and 12 March 2026, the Office of the US Trade Representative initiated two investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The first investigation involves 16 economies for structural excess capacity and production in certain manufacturing sectors, while the second investigation involves 60 economies for not adopting or effectively enforcing a ban on the importation of goods produced wholly or in part with forced labour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The US Trade Representative's Federal Register Notice on the investigation into structural excess capacity had highlighted that Singapore enjoyed a bilateral trade surplus with the US in both goods and services amounting to US$27 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has clarified that it was the US which ran a trade surplus of US$27 billion with Singapore in 2024.

sections.label: US reasons for Singapore inclusion
sections.summary: The US has not given reasons for including Singapore under the Section 301 investigations, and it is unknown if other countries share a similar perspective.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To the first and also the third question, the US has not given us reasons on why they have included Singapore under the Section 301 investigations and neither do we know if other countries might have similar perspective.

sections.label: Contact with US and Business Adaptation Grant
sections.summary: Singapore has been keeping in touch with the US, and a Business Adaptation Grant remains available to help companies understand US tariff implications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We have been keeping in touch with them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Also, there is a Business Adaptation Grant, which remains available to help companies understand the implications of the US tariffs on their businesses.

sections.label: Singapore criminalises forced labour
sections.summary: Singapore takes a strong stance and criminalises forced labour under various laws, including the Penal Code and the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: First, Singapore takes a strong stance – we also criminalise forced labour in Singapore under various laws, including the Penal Code and the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act.

sections.label: Attending the hearings
sections.summary: Singapore will be attending the hearings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The answer is yes; we will be attending the hearings.
